findings.text: U-4 is described two ways. The front matter says whether an Inactive doctor's name is shown is unknown. The body says how to show it is unknown.

cites.quote: Should the column show the doctor's name when the doctor is Inactive?
options: ["Show the name", "Show the name marked Inactive"]

findings.suggested_fix: Add an option such as 'Hide the name or show a placeholder', or reword Q-04 to ask only how the name is marked.
findings.text: Q-04 asks whether to show an Inactive doctor's name, but both options show the name. There is no real 'do not show' choice, so the question cannot test the REQ-13 assumption.

rubric_items.reason: Each of AC1-AC7 maps to a REQ. AC2 and AC6 are split into atomic REQs. The user story and past or other-patient appointments are listed as out of scope with reasons.
Each REQ states one behaviour with a checkable condition, for example the exact 'None' text, 20 per page, Asia/Kolkata and the excluded statuses.
Every known REQ cites a ticket line, and REQ-4 and REQ-12 also cite the baseline. The only assumed item, REQ-13, has a real glossary basis and an open question. No invented values are marked known.
The ticket does not clash with the baseline: the hospital time zone and the no-medical-history-in-lists rule both agree with the baseline. The PAT-8 gap is raised as Q-03 with both cites.

All questions are non-blocking, have defaults and are routed sensibly. However, Q-04's two options both show the name, so 'hide the name' is never offered, even though U-4 asks whether the name is shown at all.
Plain and readable. U-4 is worded differently in the front matter and in the body ('whether' vs 'how').
